text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. It is important to note that knee pain in children can sometimes originate from the hip. Does he experience any pain in his left hip, groin, or thigh, especially when you try to rotate his leg inward or outward?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does your son have any difficulty turning his left leg inward or outward, and does he complain of pain in his groin or thigh? I need to rule out hip pathology, as referred pain to the knee is common in conditions like Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given his age and the presentation of knee pain with a limp, I suspect referred pain from the hip. I need to see imaging to confirm if this is Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease or another condition.
